title: The wire protocol's constants live in the clients instead of wire.rs
body:
| knob | homes |
|---|---|
| protocol version 1 | `PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `viewer.rs`, `version: 1` in `script.rs`, `version < 1` and `Welcome { version: 1 }` in `compositor.rs` |
| transport 0 | `LOCAL` in `viewer.rs`, literals in `script.rs` and `compositor.rs` |
| lock bits | packed in `viewer.rs`, unpacked as `locked & 1` and `locked & 2` in `compositor.rs` |
| scale denominator 120 | `SCALE` in `script.rs`, `MAX_SCALE = 120 * 8` in `compositor.rs`, literals at four sites in `viewer.rs` |
| outbox retry 5 ms | `OUTBOX_RETRY` in `compositor.rs`, a literal in `viewer.rs` |
| `BTN_LEFT`, `KEY_LEFTCTRL`, `KEY_LEFTSHIFT`, `KEY_LEFTMETA` | `script.rs` and `compositor.rs` |

The server's handshake check amounts to `version == 0`, and nobody reads `Welcome.version`, so the lower-of-the-two negotiation in `docs/viewer.md` is not implemented. A protocol bump today can leave `decade script` behind.

## Proposal

`wire.rs` owns `VERSION`, `LOCAL`, the lock bits, the scale denominator and the evdev codes; the three clients import them. Either implement the negotiation or drop that sentence from the doc.
close_reason: Landed in 4f2cbde. wire.rs defines VERSION, LOCAL, SCALE, CAPS_LOCK, NUM_LOCK, OUTBOX_RETRY and the shared evdev codes. The server implements the negotiation in docs/viewer.md: welcome carries the lower of the two versions. Keycodes only the server uses, such as KEY_C, stay in compositor.rs.
